thread:
Marco: Heads-up — we flipped the 'shortpath' kernel selector to canary for p4d and are seeing a latency regression around seq len 8-32 (P99 up ~12%). Noticed on the canary traffic only so far :eyes:
Lia: Ugh. Any flamegraphs or nsight traces yet?
Marco: Quick trace attached from nsight run on a failed request. Key bit: sm_efficiency drops and we see more reg spills on the shortpath kernel.
Anya: Can you paste the nvprof counters? Reg spills would match.
Marco: nvprof snippet:
```
regs_used: 63
spill_store: 4123
spill_load: 4109
active_warps_per_sm: 6.2
shared_mem_per_block: 18KB
```
Kevin: Sounds like the shortpath tiling picks a larger tile to reduce thread divergence but on A100 that pushes reg pressure into spill territory. For seq=8-32 we don't amortize the extra throughput.
Lia: So immediate mitigation options? Fallback to previous kernel for short sequences? Lower tile size? Bank folding tweaks?
Marco: I pushed a canary config that lowers tile to 32x16 for shortpath and caps occupancy to 0.7 on A100. Deploy ID: canary-2026-03-17-ff12. deploy-bot shows the rollout at 10% traffic.
deploy-bot: Rollout canary-2026-03-17-ff12 -> 10% traffic (eng-runtime), started by Marco
Kevin: Prefer a conditional selector change: selector should prefer 'compact' kernel when (seqlen <= 32 AND expected_reg_use > threshold) OR occupancy > 0.68. That way we don't globally drop the shortpath.
Anya: Also look at KV cache prefetch path — prefetching a 64KB chunk into shared memory for these small sequences is causing extra SMEM pressure. If we bias prefetch to only prime headers for short requests latency wins.
Marco: Good call. We can add a prefetch size heuristic: if seqlen < 48 -> prefetch_headers_only.
Lia: Can you add a quick autotuner metric set so the kernel picker records (seqlen_histogram, occupancy_histogram, reg_use_distribution) per device? That will make the selector decisions data driven.
Kevin: Yes — and include a rolling quantile so noisy spikes don't flip the selector too often. Also add a safety margin: require 3 consecutive windows to trigger a swap.
Marco: Draft config patch I pushed to canary branch (short excerpt):
```json
{
  "selector": {
    "seqlen_thresholds": [32, 128, 512],
    "occupancy_cap": {"A100": 0.7, "V100": 0.75},
    "reg_spill_margin": 4,
    "prefetch_policy": "headers_if_short"
  }
}
```
Anya: Running a local microbench with that config — initial numbers look promising: P99 down ~6% for seq 8-32 compared to default shortpath, and no throughput hit on long sequences.
perf-bot: Uploaded flamegraphs and perf counters: https://perf.internal/redwood/canary/1765432222 — includes nvprof + trtexec outputs :white_check_mark:
Lia: Nice. If microbench is stable canary revert window should be 1h with auto-revert on >5% regression.
Marco: Agreed. I'll widen the metric capture and keep canary at 10% for 1hr then 30% if stable. If anything spikes we'll roll back.
Kevin: Longer term autotuner TODO: incorporate device-family fingerprints (sm, l2 size, register file size) and make the kernel picker cost-model run a quick simulated scoring for the top-3 kernels per seqlen bucket.
Marco: Filing a follow-up issue for the autotuner crude scoring: ENG-rt #4123. For now I'll monitor canary and post updates here. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Lia: Thanks — please include the perf-bot link in the incident ticket.
Marco: Will do.
